actors.name: Founder A
actors.private_context: Founder A believes the company should pivot to a subscription model and is frustrated with Founder B's insistence on ad-based revenue. A has been exploring buyout options with potential investors and is considering buying out Founder B.

actors.name: Founder B
actors.private_context: Founder B is committed to the ad-based revenue model and thinks Founder A's pivot idea is risky. B has been in talks with a venture capital firm about buying out Founder A's stake.

actors.name: Employees (as a group)
actors.private_context: The twelve employees are aware of the founders' disagreements through office gossip and all-hands meetings. They are concerned about job security and the company's direction, but have no direct decision-making power in a buyout.

shared_context: Tidepool is a mobile app company with two founders and twelve employees. The founders have been publicly at odds over strategy since spring 2026. A buyout would involve one founder purchasing the other's shares and the departing founder leaving the company. The company has no board of directors; the founders hold equal equity and decision-making power. The employees have no formal role in a buyout decision.

starting_events.description: The simulation begins. The founders are at odds, and no buyout has been announced yet.

resolution: Resolve YES if, before the cutoff, the persistent event history shows that either Founder A or Founder B publicly announces to the employees that a buyout of one founder's shares by the other has been agreed upon and will proceed. Otherwise resolve NO at the cutoff.
